title: Introduce intent-aware onboarding flags and compact release abridger
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Model intake metadata today focuses on schema and capability tags but lacks a first-class, compact signal for the "intent" of an onboarded model (primary use: generation, embeddings, reranking, tool-calling). This gap makes it hard for downstream automation (routing, profiling, targeted evals) to pick and prioritize change notes and performance baselines.

This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) an intent-aware metadata flagset attached to model intake and profile manifests, and 2) a small release abridger tool that synthesizes compact release notes tailored to the intents present in a model version delta. The abridger yields a short, human-readable changelog headline + intent-scoped bullets suitable for release dashboards and email digests.

What changed (high level):
- Add new model metadata field `intents` (enum list) with accepted values: generation, embeddings, reranking, tool_calling, summarization, dialog. Validation is enforced at intake and via the onboard linter.
- Add migration helper `scripts/migrate/add-intent-heuristics.py` to gently seed intents for existing profiles using profile tags and perf signals. The migration is opt-in.
- Implement `tools/release_abridger/` CLI that consumes a model delta (old/new profile snapshots) and emits a compact JSON + plain-text synopsis focused on intents changed. It uses simple scoring heuristics to pick top-3 impact lines per intent.
- Wire the abridger into the onboard CI hook so nightly model-batch uploads generate a draft abridged changelog artifact for review.
- Tests: unit tests for intent validation, migration heuristics, and abridger scoring. Integration test that runs abridger end-to-end with sample snapshots.

Checklist:

Review conversation summary: 
- Arjun Desai: "Nice direction. Can you clarify how intents interact with the existing capability tags? We need deterministic precedence for routing decisions."
  - Maya: "Intents are a lightweight routing hint orthogonal to capability tags; added precedence rules in schema comments and linter clarifications (intents take precedence for quick routing while capability tags remain authoritative for compatibility checks)."
- Lena Fischer: "Score logic looks heuristic-heavy — add a short doc explaining scoring weights and a flag to opt for a conservative mode."
  - Maya: "Added `--conservative` to the CLI and documented weights in abridger/README.md; integration tests now assert conservative output is shorter."
- Noah Kim: "CI failed on lint initially; looks like a formatting issue in examples."
  - Maya: "Fixed formatting and added linter exception comments where needed; re-ran CI."
- Arjun Desai (approval): "Approach and API look good; documented backward compatibility. Approved."

CI details: 
- Initial CI run: lint failure in examples (fixed in a2)
- Subsequent run: unit tests passed, integration passed, coverage unchanged (+0.4%). Final status: pass.

Merge: Squash-merged into main after approvals and green CI.

Notes on backward compatibility and rollout: 
- New `intents` field is optional for existing onboards; onboard linter will recommend an intent or `unspecified` when absent.
- Migration helper is opt-in and emits a report; we do not auto-tag older profiles.
- Abridger outputs are additive artifacts stored under `releases/abridged/` and do not replace full changelogs.

Operational follow-ups (tracked outside this PR): 
- Hook abridger artifacts into Console release cards (ENG-2175).
- Add a per-tenant policy to force intent on private installs (security/compliance ask).

Overall impact: Provides a compact, intent-scoped summarization layer that helps product, release engineering, and customers get a faster, focused view of model changes that matter to their workflows.
